what_to_detect: A prevention effect meets a damage event it applies to and prevents all or part of it (result prevented, replaced or updated on a rewrite whose replacement is a prevention effect). In Forge a prevention effect does not always report result 'prevented': only a Prevent$ True replacement (Fog, 'prevent all damage') does; a shield or PreventionEffect$ replacement (PreventDamage shields, Circle of Protection, Vigor, Daunting Defender) reports 'replaced' when it absorbs all the damage and 'updated' when it absorbs part, and damage replacements that prevent nothing (doubling, redirection) report the same 'replaced'/'updated'. rewrite_event takes one result value and cannot restrict to prevention effects, so any single value tags real preventions as near misses.
near_miss: A prevention effect meets a damage event and prevents none of it (result not_replaced); damage the effect does not apply to produces no rewrite record.
record_fields: the acting replacement line's script (Prevent$ True / PreventionEffect$) via the sidecar, or the runtime shield the Fog and PreventDamage APIs create

what_to_detect: A prevention effect, still within its duration and not used up, prevents damage it applies to. In Forge a prevention effect does not always report result 'prevented': only a Prevent$ True replacement (Fog, 'prevent all damage') does; a shield or PreventionEffect$ replacement (PreventDamage shields, Circle of Protection, Vigor, Daunting Defender) reports 'replaced' when it absorbs all the damage and 'updated' when it absorbs part, and damage replacements that prevent nothing (doubling, redirection) report the same 'replaced'/'updated'. rewrite_event takes one result value and cannot restrict to prevention effects, so any single value tags real preventions as near misses.
near_miss: Damage dealt after the effect's duration ended meets no effect and produces no rewrite record, so the near miss counted is a prevention that prevented nothing (not_replaced).
record_fields: the acting replacement line's script (Prevent$ True / PreventionEffect$) via the sidecar, or the runtime shield the Fog and PreventDamage APIs create
